newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa's Cross to head forex for central bank.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa's Cross to head forex for central bank.

text.p: South Africa's newest deputy governor at the Reserve Bank, James Cross, will head all foreign exchange and capital markets for the central bank, Governor Chris Stals said on Monday night.
Stals said in a statement the bank's exchange control, international banking as well as money and capital market departments would fall under Cross.
"(He) will be responsible for the bank's domestic money and capital market and foreign exchange market operations," the statement said.

Cross, whom Stals described as an "experienced international banking and financial market operator", was appointed as one of the bank's three deputy governors late last year, effective from January 1997.

He served as general manager of the central bank's gold and foreign exchange department from April 1987 until July 1995. Until his reappointment, he had worked in a private research and consulting business in London.

The two other deputy governors of the bank are Chris de Swardt, responsible for domestic financial operations and internal administration, and Timothy Thahane, who handles economic services and relations with other African countries, the World Bank and the International Monetary Fund.
